case.summary: Undo without a selector undoes the newest operation.
Undo without a selector never undoes an undo entry.
Undo of an operation by number leaves later operations in place.
The report of an undo carries its own operation number.
Undo of a change of several files restores every file.
Undo to an operation reverts every later operation as one undo.
Undo of one file restores only that file.
Undo of selected paths of one operation restores those paths only.
Redo of an undo applies the operation again.
Redo after a later change of the same file reports the conflict.
Redo of an operation that is not an undo reports nothing to redo.
Undo with an empty journal reports nothing to undo.
Undo of an unknown operation changes nothing.
A second undo of the same operation reports nothing to undo.
A preview creates no operation, so there is nothing to undo.
Undo after a later change of the same file fails and changes nothing.
The choice report is the default of on_conflict.
Undo with force restores the content despite a later change.
Undo with force keeps the current content, so its redo restores it.
Undo with include_later also undoes the later change.
Undo with abort changes nothing on a conflict.
Undo of a partial entry fails unless partial asks for the remaining items.
History lists the operations, newest first.
History shows an undone operation as undone.
History filtered by state lists only the matching operations.
History of one path lists only the operations that touched it.
Reading programs create no journal entry.
History records the scope of an undo.
The report of a change has the operation number and no expiry member.
The report of an undo has no expiry member.
The report of a history query has no expiry member.
An entry beyond the step limit expires and cannot be undone.
Undo to an operation fails and changes nothing when the selection has an expired entry.
An entry older than the age limit expires on the test clock.
The oldest entry expires when the kept content exceeds the size limit.
A pinned entry survives lowered limits and can still be undone.
Releasing a pin within the limits expires nothing; the entry can be undone.
A change with the journal disabled is reported as irreversible and cannot be undone.
A change on a volume below the space reserve is made without a copy and reported as no_space_for_copy.
An operation larger than the limit of one entry is made without a copy and reported as too_large_for_journal.
An operation larger than the size budget is made without a copy by default.
With oversize keep, an operation larger than the size budget is kept and can be undone.
